title: Comparing tension-type headache, migraine and cluster headache
intro: Headache types overlap, and location or severity alone cannot establish a diagnosis. Tension-type headache and migraine are common; cluster headache is less common but very disabling. A new or changing pattern needs its own assessment.

sections.heading: Tension-type pattern
paragraphs: Often a pressing or tightening pain on both sides, mild to moderate and not substantially worsened by ordinary activity. Marked vomiting is less typical. Symptoms still deserve help when frequent or disruptive.

sections.heading: Migraine pattern
paragraphs: Often moderate to severe, sometimes throbbing and aggravated by activity, with nausea or sensitivity to light and sound. Some people have aura, but many do not. New neurological symptoms should not automatically be labeled aura. Bring your medicine list and previous results; ask which findings would change the plan.

sections.heading: Cluster pattern
paragraphs: Very severe one-sided pain around an eye may occur with tearing, nasal symptoms and restlessness in repeated bouts. Prompt diagnosis matters because suitable acute treatment differs from ordinary painkillers; a painful red eye also has other urgent causes. Agree how benefit and adverse effects will be checked before changing treatment.

sections.heading: Getting the right plan
paragraphs: Record timing, duration, associated symptoms and medicine days. Treatment may involve appropriate acute medicines and prevention; frequent analgesic use can sustain headache. Do not borrow someone’s migraine medicine solely because the pain sounds similar. Choose a routine you can maintain, and discuss barriers such as cost, work or language.

sections.heading: Warning signs
paragraphs: Sudden maximal severe pain, weakness, confusion, fever with stiff neck, vision loss or significant head injury requires urgent assessment. New severe headache in pregnancy or after birth also needs prompt care, even with a history of migraine.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira’s repeated headaches include nausea and light sensitivity. She records the pattern and asks for assessment instead of assuming every headache is tension.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben has severe eye-area pain and tearing. He seeks prompt assessment rather than repeatedly taking standard tablets without a diagnosis.
